rules.key_semantics: English source text is the key; en renders the key verbatim
rules.dictionary_merge: src/i18n/zh/*.ts spread order parsed from src/i18n/index.tsx; later spread wins
rules.reference_gate: only files calling useI18n() count as i18n consumers; local `t` shadows excluded by scope analysis
rules.static_key: first argument is exactly one string literal (or a template without ${})
rules.expression_keys: every depth-0 string literal in a ternary/expression first argument; comparison operands and top-level '+' concatenation excluded
rules.dynamic_resolution: const object/array literals, indexed const lookups, property-name pools (same file + direct imports), local helper-function string literals; candidates only
rules.dead_key: dictionary key with no static/expression reference; total is the disjoint sum of dictionary-only, literal-elsewhere and dynamic-candidate-only layers
rules.tokenizer: TS tokenizer that splices ${...} template interpolations as code, skips JSX tag slashes and JSX-prose quote pairs, and treats regex literals contextually
rules.value_checks: value == key; placeholder sets between key and value; empty value
rules.tree_b: same dictionary/reference scan gated on evidence of an i18n mechanism

limitations: dynamic t(expr) keys that only exist at runtime cannot be statically resolved; unresolved call sites are listed
dictionary keys can be hit by backend-provided strings at runtime (e.g. status values); dead-key classification is static
JSX text nodes written without t() are outside the reference scope of this audit
dynamic-resolution candidate keys are a superset heuristic and are reported as low confidence
the tokenizer is a heuristic, not a full TSX parser (JSX prose quotes, regex literals, template interpolations are handled by context rules)
tree B has no i18n layer, so A-vs-B zh value comparison is structurally empty
